Why the line closed

Rail services on the Kessel Valley line will be suspended for three weeks from Monday while engineers replace a corroded section of track near Harrow Bridge, the regional transport authority announced on Tuesday.

The line carries about 1,200 commuters a day between Harrow Bridge and the coast, and replacement buses will run every twenty minutes during the morning and evening peaks, the authority said in a statement.

Engineers found the corrosion during a routine inspection last month and recommended that the affected rail be replaced before the winter timetable begins.

Engineers found the corrosion during a routine inspection last month and recommended that the affected rail be replaced before the winter timetable begins, when heavier freight traffic is expected on the route.

Councillors from three towns along the line asked the authority to keep fares unchanged for season ticket holders while the buses are running, arguing that the longer journeys already cost commuters time.

A spokesperson for the authority said the work would be carried out in two shifts and that noise limits agreed with residents would apply, with the loudest operations scheduled for daytime hours only.

Passengers can check the replacement timetable on station noticeboards and at the authority's information desk, and accessible vehicles will be available on request at every stop along the route.
